scope: First hardware step of the DPMAIF data path: the two clock gates, the device tree node and a read-only reconnaissance driver that samples registers without writing any.

images.content: first attempt; probe failed with -ENOENT on the dpmaif-main clock
extends the clock provider's onecell size to cover the DPMAIF ids; probe and sampling succeed

implementation.clocks: ifrao3 gate at 0xa4/0xa8/0xac shift 3 (CLK_IFRAO_DPMAIF, id 39) and ifrao4 at 0xc0/0xc4/0xc8 shift 26 (CLK_IFRAO_DPMAIF_MAIN, id 74), both CLK_IGNORE_UNUSED so LK's state is preserved
implementation.dt_node: dpmaif@10014000 with the four vendor register ranges, GIC_SPI 209, both clocks and the existing infracfg phandle; disabled by default and enabled only by the image builder
implementation.driver: ccci-dpmaif.c maps the four windows, the infracfg regmap, the interrupt number and both clocks; it writes no register and requests no interrupt. The sample attribute enables both clocks for one read and releases them again
implementation.formatter: ccci-dpmaif-format.c is split out so the exact rendering is unit tested on the host

hardware.probe: op6893-dpmaif 10014000.dpmaif: dpmaif observed: irq=242, 4 blocks mapped, no register written
hardware.stability: three consecutive reads while the MD was held at lk-on returned identical values
reading: both gates enable and the parent rate is 156 MHz, so the clock path and the map are real
the uplink descriptors and channel status are zero because nothing has initialised the data path yet; this is the expected pre-init state, not a fault
infra_ctrl reads 0x3000: the two-bit busy field is 3 and the MD to AP wakeup bit is still latched, which is the state LK left behind
the SRAM window holds non-zero residual words, so the block is powered and readable rather than stuck

bug_found_on_hardware.cause: clk-mt6893-pmif.c sizes its onecell array as CLK_IFRAO_CCIF2_MD + 1 = 70, so the DPMAIF ids 39 and 74 were outside the array and of_clk_hw_onecell_get returned nothing for 74
bug_found_on_hardware.fix: take the maximum of the enabled id ranges instead of the last CCIF id
bug_found_on_hardware.note: the host tests could not see this: it only shows up when the provider and the consumer are both live

open.irq: the DTS requests GIC_SPI 209 and the live device tree confirms <0 209 4>, but platform_get_irq reports virq 242; the hwirq column of /proc/interrupts cannot be compared without requesting the interrupt, so this must be confirmed by the step that installs the handler
open.no_data_path: nothing here moves a packet; the UL/DL descriptor rings, the BAT and PIT tables and the interrupt handler are still unimplemented
